title: A strategy the student owns
statement: Name a strategy's steps in words that work on any text, not one app's mechanics, and present it as the student's own tool for when a text gets hard.
detail: A content review of a reference reading lesson asked for a step's verb to change from 'tap' to 'find', because finding is what a student will do in any text, not just in the app (`grade3-reading/artifacts/feedback-aladdin-2026-08-25/feedback-text.txt`, line 21), and the course's register lists the reworded steps as met (`grade3-reading/artifacts/criteria-register.csv`, line 115). A 285-criterion review profile asks that every strategy be framed as the student's to use when the text gets hard; on two lessons that framing was missing (`grade3-reading/artifacts/peter-pan-standing-2026-09-11/readiness-l5-2026-09-17/sim-review/agent-A-D1-D4.md`, lines 92-103).
against: The same review rated the framing criterion advisory, since students already run the steps alone in the independent task (`grade3-reading/artifacts/peter-pan-standing-2026-09-11/readiness-l5-2026-09-17/sim-review/agent-A-D1-D4.md`, line 103), and the gap was carried to a register as a note, not fixed (`grade3-reading/artifacts/peter-pan-standing-2026-09-11/readiness-l5-2026-09-17/L5-REVIEW-GAPS-2026-09-17.md`, line 12).

evidence.quote: because ‘find’ captures what they will need to do in any text (not just on this app)
Every strategy is explicitly framed as 'yours to use when the text gets hard'
retiring "hunt for keywords" (many texts have no clean keyword) and "reread and tap" -> "reread and find" ("find" names what a reader does, not what a finger does).
INFER is framed exactly that way at its introduction in L2
